title: The Quiet Bridge
premise: In the river town of Vellamont, 1873, Cyrus Reyes has spent three years as an invisible apprentice to Master Aldous Fen, completing a county atlas that secretly records every family displaced by the army's new bridge project. When soldiers requisition the workshop and seize Fen's ledger of names, Cyrus learns the atlas itself is evidence—Fen died protecting it, and the army wants the remaining plates destroyed. Hiding in plain sight as a hired copyist for the very officers hunting his master's work, Cyrus must finish the final maps and smuggle them across the occupied town to the one judge willing to hear the families' case. In the end he chooses truth over safety, testifying under his own name at last, and the atlas is published not as Fen's monument but as the town's shared memory—with Cyrus listed as its author.
about_author: Felix Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing municipal maps and land disputes in small river towns. The Quiet Bridge is a novel born from the marginalia he found there—the unsigned notes of people history almost forgot.

chapters.title: The Weight of Blank Paper
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Opening in the workshop three days after Master Fen's quiet death, Cyrus inks coastlines by candlelight and hides the unfinished plates beneath the floorboards. Emotional beat: grief expressed only through precision; he has never once said his master's name aloud since the funeral.

chapters.title: Requisition Orders
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Soldiers post notices on the bridge: the town is requisitioned, all records and ledgers to be surrendered within the week. Cyrus watches neighbors line up to hand over papers, clutching Fen's ledger of displaced families under his coat. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Holds
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, night scene. He reads Fen's ledger by lamplight—names, dates, payments refused—and understands the atlas was never just cartography but testimony. Beat: the apprentice inherits a purpose he never asked for.

chapters.title: The Officer Who Draws
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Captain Elise Marchand, who leads the requisition, visits the workshop and reveals she sketches landscapes herself; she offers Cyrus paid work copying military survey charts. Beat: dangerous flattery—he accepts to stay close to the enemy.

chapters.title: Invisible Hands
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Working under Marchand's roof by day, finishing Fen's plates by night, Cyrus nearly burns the workshop when a lamp tips. Old Widow Sable, the cook, covers for him without being asked. Beat: first thread of found family.

chapters.title: Sable's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Widow Sable's POV. She recognizes Fen's ink stains on Cyrus's cuffs and quietly feeds him, telling stories of the families the ledger names—including her own drowned ferry trade. Beat: Cyrus realizes he is not alone in remembering.

chapters.title: A Map Is a Promise
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. He discovers Fen's final annotation on the last plate: coordinates marking where the army falsified the river survey to justify the bridge route. Beat: awe and terror—the atlas can prove fraud, if it reaches the right hands.

chapters.title: The Judge at Millbrook
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A traveling assize judge, Honora Quill, will sit in Millbrook in nineteen days—the only court outside army jurisdiction. Cyrus calculates the distance against the pace of his own hands. Beat: hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: Marchand's Doubt
chapters.summary: Marchand's POV. She reviews the seized ledgers and finds gaps too clean to be honest; her superior, Colonel Vasse, orders the workshop 'cleared' after the week ends. Beat: her loyalty to the army begins to crack against what she sees.

chapters.title: Copyist's Gambit
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. He hides finished map sections inside blank military chart stock, passing them through Marchand's own dispatch crates. Sable sews the first bundle into a flour sack. Beat: cunning rising into confidence—too much confidence.

chapters.title: The Search
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Vasse's men tear through the workshop hunting Fen's hidden plates; they find the floorboard cache empty because Sable moved it hours earlier. Beat: near-catastrophe, and Cyrus learns someone else is protecting him.

chapters.title: What Sable Buried
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She reveals she hid the plates in the old ferry house and confesses her son was among the families Fen recorded. Beat: grief shared becomes loyalty declared—she is in, whatever it costs.

chapters.title: Vasse's Summons
chapters.summary: Marchand's POV. Vasse suspects a leak inside his own command and orders Marchand to identify the copyist or be charged herself. Beat: the hunter becomes the hunted; she begins reading Fen's ledger in secret.

chapters.title: Nineteen Becomes Nine
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A flooded road closes the Millbrook crossing; the judge's sitting moves up, and the final plate—the fraudulent survey overlay—is still uninked. Beat: despair; his hands shake for the first time.

chapters.title: Two Draftsmen
chapters.summary: Cyrus and Marchand, alternating POV. Marchand finds Cyrus working past midnight on a plate that matches nothing in the official survey. Instead of arresting him, she asks him to teach her Fen's hatching technique. Beat: trust offered across enemy lines.

chapters.title: The Ferry House
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Retrieving the plates before dawn, Cyrus and Sable are spotted by a patrol; Sable takes a soldier's baton blow covering his escape. Beat: guilt and fury—his invisibility has been costing other people their safety.

chapters.title: Confession at the Bridge
chapters.summary: Marchand's POV. She confronts Vasse with the altered survey figures; he dismisses her and signs the workshop demolition order. Beat: she chooses truth over uniform, burning her own commission letter.

chapters.title: The Last Plate
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. With Marchand standing guard and Sable binding wounds, Cyrus inks the final overlay as soldiers hammer the workshop door. They escape through the coal cellar as the demolition crew arrives. Beat: climax of craft—the work is finished as the world that held it burns.

chapters.title: Millbrook
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. At the assize, Cyrus presents the atlas and speaks his full name for the first time in the novel, entering Fen's ledger into record. Marchand corroborates the falsified survey. Beat: the invisible man made visible; loyalty to truth fulfilled.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Judge Quill's ruling arrives: the bridge route is voided pending honest resurvey, and the displaced families are owed restitution. Vasse is recalled in disgrace. Beat: justice, imperfect but real; the town exhales.

chapters.title: What the Fire Left
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. He walks the ashes of the workshop and recovers Fen's brass compass from the rubble. Sable insists he move into the ferry house; Marchand, dismissed from the army, asks to apprentice in reverse—to learn from him. Beat: mourning braided with gratitude; found family solidifies.

chapters.title: The Quiet Bridge
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, epilogue one year later. The corrected atlas is printed with both names on the title page—Fen's above, his below—and the new bridge, honestly surveyed, opens quietly without ceremony. Beat: memory kept not in monuments but in shared work; Cyrus finally belongs somewhere, and to someone.
